subject: Polity
sub_topic: Article 13 — judicial review and void laws

concepts.name: Article 13(1) - Pre-Constitutional Laws and Inconsistency
key_dimensions: Definition of 'laws in force' - includes customs, usages, ordinances, regulations, notifications
Doctrine of eclipse vs. void ab initio - pre-constitutional laws are eclipsed, not void
Revival of eclipsed laws after constitutional amendments (e.g., Zamindari Abolition cases)
Distinction between Article 13(1) and 13(2) regarding temporal application

concepts.name: Article 13(2) - Post-Constitutional Laws and Void Ab Initio
key_dimensions: Laws made after Constitution commencement are void ab initio if inconsistent
No doctrine of eclipse applicable to post-constitutional laws
Difference in treatment: pre-constitutional (eclipsed) vs post-constitutional (void)
State cannot make laws that take away or abridge fundamental rights

concepts.name: Article 13(3) - Definition of 'Law' and Its Scope
key_dimensions: Inclusive definition: ordinances, orders, bye-laws, rules, regulations, notifications, customs, usages
Judicial expansion through case law (e.g., treaty obligations, executive actions)
Exclusions and grey areas - private agreements, contracts by State
UPSC trap: What constitutes 'law' for Article 13 purposes vs. Article 265

concepts.name: Article 13(4) - Non-Application to Constitutional Amendments
key_dimensions: Constitutional amendments under Article 368 are not 'law' under Article 13
Golak Nath case (1967) - amendments are 'law', hence subject to Article 13
Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) - overruled Golak Nath, but introduced Basic Structure
Current position: Amendments can be challenged only on basic structure grounds, not Article 13

concepts.name: Doctrine of Eclipse - Mechanism and Application
key_dimensions: Only applicable to pre-constitutional laws under Article 13(1)
Law becomes dormant/inoperative but not dead - can revive if FR is removed
Bhikaji Narain case (1955) - established doctrine of eclipse
Effect on persons: non-citizens can be prosecuted under eclipsed law, citizens cannot

concepts.name: Doctrine of Severability (Article 13 context)
key_dimensions: Invalid portion can be severed if separable from valid portion
Tests: textual severability, substantial severability, policy severability
A.K. Gopalan case and R.M.D. Chamarbaugwala case - leading judgments
UPSC trap: When severability is NOT possible - inseverable provisions

concepts.name: Judicial Review - Power and Scope under Article 13
key_dimensions: Article 13 is the foundation of judicial review in India
Supreme Court and High Courts' power to declare laws void
Limitations: cannot review on policy grounds, only constitutional validity
Comparison with US judicial review - Marbury vs Madison parallel

concepts.name: 'State' Definition under Article 12 and Its Impact on Article 13
key_dimensions: Article 13 applies to laws made by 'State' as defined in Article 12
Expansion of 'State' through judicial interpretation affects Article 13 scope
Actions of instrumentalities and agencies of State subject to Article 13
UPSC trap: Private bodies performing public functions - when Article 13 applies

concepts.name: Constitutional Amendments vs. Ordinary Laws under Article 13
key_dimensions: Article 13(4) specifically excludes constitutional amendments from definition of 'law'
Evolution: Shankari Prasad → Sajjan Singh → Golak Nath → Kesavananda Bharati
Current position: Amendments immune from Article 13 but subject to basic structure
9th Schedule laws - initially immune, now subject to judicial review post-Coelho case (2007)

concepts.name: Void Ab Initio vs. Prospective Invalidation
key_dimensions: General rule: unconstitutional law is void from inception (ab initio)
Exception: Court may declare law invalid prospectively in certain cases
Deep Chand case - prospective overruling to avoid chaos
UPSC trap: Circumstances when courts use prospective invalidation

concepts.name: Executive Actions and Administrative Orders under Article 13
key_dimensions: Whether executive actions constitute 'law' under Article 13(3)
Distinction between legislative and executive actions
Minerva Mills case - executive actions can be challenged under Article 13
Delegated legislation and subordinate legislation - subject to Article 13

concepts.name: Customs and Usages as 'Law' under Article 13
key_dimensions: Article 13(3)(a) explicitly includes customs and usages having force of law
Personal law customs violating fundamental rights can be challenged
Narasu Appa Mali case controversy - personal laws and Article 13
Recent developments: Triple Talaq case and Article 13 application

concepts.name: Article 13 and Directive Principles - Conflict Resolution
key_dimensions: Article 13 protects FRs; DPSPs under Part IV may conflict
Champakam Dorairajan case - FRs prevail over DPSPs
Constitutional amendments (1st, 4th, 25th, 42nd) to give effect to DPSPs
Minerva Mills - balance between Articles 14, 19, 31 and 39(b), (c)

concepts.name: 9th Schedule and Article 13 - Immunity and Judicial Review
key_dimensions: 9th Schedule created by 1st Amendment to protect land reform laws from Article 13
Original position: laws in 9th Schedule immune from judicial review
I.R. Coelho case (2007) - 9th Schedule laws can be reviewed on basic structure grounds
UPSC trap: Post-Kesavananda amendments to 9th Schedule are reviewable

concepts.name: Inconsistency and Repugnancy under Article 13
key_dimensions: Test for inconsistency: direct conflict, impossibility of simultaneous compliance
Partial vs. complete inconsistency - effect on law's validity
Distinction between Article 13 inconsistency and Article 254 repugnancy
Degree of inconsistency required for invalidation under Article 13

concepts.name: Article 13 and Emergency Provisions - Suspension of Enforcement
key_dimensions: Article 358 - automatic suspension of Article 19 during National Emergency
Article 359 - President can suspend right to move court for FR enforcement
Laws made during emergency and Article 13 scrutiny post-emergency
UPSC trap: Article 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even under Article 359

concepts.name: Territorial Application of Article 13
key_dimensions: Article 13 applies to entire territory of India including J&K (post-Article 370 abrogation)
Laws made by Parliament and State Legislatures both covered
Union Territory laws and Article 13 application
Extra-territorial operation of laws and Article 13 challenges

concepts.name: Article 13 and International Treaties/Conventions
key_dimensions: Whether international treaties constitute 'law' under Article 13
Vishaka case - international conventions used to fill legislative vacuum
Treaties require domestic legislation to have force of law in India
UPSC trap: Unimplemented treaties cannot be directly enforced but can aid interpretation

concepts.name: Burden of Proof and Presumption of Constitutionality
key_dimensions: Presumption that laws are constitutional - burden on challenger
Standard of proof required to declare law void under Article 13
Reasonable classification doctrine and presumption of constitutionality
When presumption is rebutted - manifest arbitrariness test

concepts.name: Article 13 and Fundamental Duties (Article 51A)
key_dimensions: Whether laws enforcing Fundamental Duties can override FRs under Article 13
Relationship between Article 13 and Article 51A
Courts' approach: FDs cannot dilute FRs protected by Article 13
UPSC trap: FDs are not enforceable but can be used for interpreting laws under Article 13
